claims.statement: Implementing Regulation 2024/2956 prescribes interlinked standard templates for registers covering contractual arrangements with direct ICT third-party providers.
Only 6.5% of almost 1,000 registers in the 2024 ESA dry run passed all 116 data-quality checks, directly evidencing preparation difficulty.
KNF required a second 2025 submission stage for entities that had not filed or whose registers were rejected by EBA validation.
KNF also supplies an official spreadsheet form and instructions, making internal spreadsheet completion a free substitute.
Warsaw-based DAPR already sells DORA Register with automation, validation, provider dependencies, supply-chain data, and annual prices from EUR 2,000 to EUR 8,000 by external ICT-contract count.
Vendorica markets AI contract extraction, a live vendor-contract-asset graph, reconciled DORA exports, and a EUR 899 monthly professional plan, directly overlapping the proposed differentiation.
ReportAct offers a DORA register and incident product at EUR 299 per month per location plus EUR 7 per active supplier, adding another transparent price anchor.

contrary_evidence: DAPR's Warsaw-based DORA Register is an exact local substitute with automated reporting, validation, provider dependencies, supply-chain handling, and EUR 2,000-8,000 annual pricing.
Vendorica already combines AI agreement extraction with the live vendor, contract, and asset graph proposed as the compounding advantage.
ReportAct supplies another transparent, lower-entry DORA register product at EUR 299 per month per location plus a supplier fee.
KNF and the ESAs provide official forms, rules, examples, and validation materials, allowing capable GRC teams to maintain the register internally.
The 2024 dry-run failure rate proves pain but not durable software demand; error rates may improve after the first reporting cycles.

economics.acquisition_route: Secure one Polish audit or compliance partner, offer free technical validation on non-confidential sample data, and convert a five-entity portfolio before building broader DORA modules.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Illustrative, not validated: 300 entities at 24,000 PLN ARR yields 7.2m PLN ARR. At 25% EBITDA, 4x EBITDA, and 70% founder ownership, founder equity is about 5.04m PLN in years 7-10. Achieving 300 regulated customers against exact incumbents requires repeatable partner distribution that is not evidenced.
economics.founder_time: 3-5 hours per day for a narrow validator and pilot; use a contracted DORA specialist and avoid bespoke consulting, while reserving daytime availability for partner and security reviews.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Inference: 68-82% after secure hosting, evidence review, partner share, and contracted DORA expertise; margin falls sharply if contract classification remains human-intensive.
economics.payback: Unknown. A target of 12-18 months is plausible only if one partner supplies several entities and security review does not create a long unpaid implementation; no partner economics or sales-cycle evidence exists.
economics.pricing: Validation hypothesis: 12,000-36,000 PLN annual base per entity plus fixed onboarding or human-verified exception work; transparent competitors range from roughly EUR 2,000-10,788 annually for relevant plans.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Registers must be maintained as arrangements change and recur in reporting cycles, but annual filing may be handled internally once learned unless continuous contract and provider workflows deliver value.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: A permissioned library of verified provider identities, contract-field mappings, service categories, and extraction corrections could reduce repeat work, although DORA Register and Vendorica already build overlapping provider and contract graphs
fingerprint.customer: Small and mid-sized DORA-scope financial entities and outsourced compliance or audit teams that maintain fragmented ICT-contract records and are not already served by a group GRC platform
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Acquire portfolios through Polish IT auditors and compliance outsourcers, using a free validation or preflight tool as the lead-in; no partner commitment is evidenced
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Evidence-linked contract extraction, entity and LEI resolution, hierarchy checks, subcontractor requests, rejected-cell repair, versioning, and ESA-format export sold as a focused annual data-utility subscription
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: The regulated entity or its outsourced compliance provider pays an annual subscription and onboarding fee for an accurate, reviewable, regulator-ready register and contract change workflow
fingerprint.problem_trigger: An ICT contract is signed, renewed, amended, rejected in regulatory validation, or included in the annual register cycle and its provider, service, entity, function, identifier, and supply-chain data must reconcile across the prescribed templates

founder_fit: Entity resolution, document extraction, data validation, and finance context closely match the founder's skills.
A synthetic-data validator and one partner pilot can be built part-time without a public personal brand.
Partner-led distribution can reduce continuous founder networking if a partner is secured.
Confidential-contract security review, legal interpretation, and regulated procurement require specialist support and may strain a 5-hour daily limit.
risks: Exact incumbent overlap makes customer acquisition and differentiation difficult.
A contract or entity-resolution error can contaminate a regulatory submission and create liability.
Security review and regulated procurement can exceed the founder's part-time capacity and initial capital.
Compliance partners may capture most economics or prefer their own spreadsheet and consulting process.
The product could drift into bespoke GRC consulting with lower margin and heavy meetings.

structure.control_point: the contract-review and reporting-quality gate at which an ICT arrangement must reconcile across the DORA register templates
structure.critical_dependency: security-approved access to confidential contracts and materially better extraction or partner economics than exact incumbent register products

thesis: Test a narrow, partner-delivered contract-ingestion and register-quality service for smaller DORA-scope financial entities whose registers are still assembled from fragmented contracts and spreadsheets. Official dry-run and Polish resubmission evidence establishes real data-quality pain, but an exact Warsaw competitor and graph-based European rivals already automate the register at transparent prices. A viable entry must therefore win through a compliance or audit partner, high-accuracy evidence-linked contract extraction, rapid repair of rejected data, and security acceptable for confidential agreements—not through template generation alone. Partner access, budgets, procurement duration, and extraction accuracy remain unvalidated.
title: DORA Contract-to-Register Data Utility
uncertainties: Number and budget of reachable Polish or EU entities not already served by a group tool, DAPR, or a broader GRC platform.
Whether an audit or compliance partner will resell the product rather than use an incumbent or build the workflow.
Security, data-residency, insurance, and procurement requirements for confidential contracts.
Extraction accuracy and human-review cost across real multilingual contract sets.
Contract-change frequency and willingness to pay for continuous maintenance after successful annual filing.
